Unknown-9.jpg.used: The design method is to define a target trajectory/force range for a powered human-carrying ornithopter and evaluate candidate wing actions.
Unknown-9.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: No engine, mass budget or coefficient table is specified by Stanley.
Unknown-9.jpg.engineering_completion: The model uses the supplied 55 kg pilot, 173.9 kg dry mass including pilot, 3.6 kg initial fuel and finite 16 kW shaft cap.

Unknown-10.jpg.used: Straight and level flapping flight has cyclic lift/thrust and small undulating speed/trajectory variations; recovery lift may be intermittent at low speed.
Unknown-10.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: Wake sketches are explanatory, not dimensions for the aircraft.
Unknown-10.jpg.engineering_completion: The simulator does not prescribe the path; strip aerodynamics and coupled dynamics produce the cyclic forces.

Unknown-11.jpg.used: Low speed downstroke lasts longer than recovery, while cruise tends to equal timing; wing/body/spring resonance reduces inertial power.
Unknown-11.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: Marginal revisions are not treated as exact equations.
Unknown-11.jpg.engineering_completion: kinematics.mjs implements theta=phi-b*sin(phi), with b fixed per run; the helper spring/inertia model stores and returns energy without creating net power.

Unknown-12.jpg.used: Wing/body inertias form a resonant mass-spring system; fore/aft wing motion changes centre-of-lift separation and produces body pitching. The wing action separates inner arm wing and outer hand wing; recovery closes/reduces span.
Unknown-12.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: The prose gives qualitative action, not all linkage dimensions.
Unknown-12.jpg.engineering_completion: The model uses fixed-amplitude stroke, twist, sweep, exposure and camber curves and a conventional tail to complete the mechanism.

Unknown-13.jpg.used: Incidence and camber are distinct variables; bird wings share basic parts with varying proportions.
Unknown-13.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: The goshawk camber percentages are an example and not mute-swan specifications.
Unknown-13.jpg.engineering_completion: Inner/outer camber bases and amplitudes are supplied assumptions; geometry renders curved fabric separately from twist.

Unknown-14.jpg.used: Inner arm sections are about 5-6 percent thick; the outer hand wing is a thin slotted curved plate with high lift/drag, partly closing on recovery. Conventional tail/rudder or weight-shift controls are compatible with a mechanical ornithopter. Takeoff swans use greater hand motion and frequency.
Unknown-14.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: No validated manned takeoff mechanism is specified.
Unknown-14.jpg.engineering_completion: The visual aircraft has a light frame, seated pilot, engine/transmission, tailplane, fin/rudder and three wheels; physics uses the supplied finite power and larger outer stroke.

Unknown-15.jpg.used: Power requirement starts from D*V glide work plus induced, acceleration, vertical-cycle and wing-inertial terms; a spring can exchange but not supply net propulsion energy.
Unknown-15.jpg.excluded_or_uncertain: Appendices and revised equations are missing.
Unknown-15.jpg.engineering_completion: Energy counters integrate actual shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, damping/transmission heat and control work; motor-off coasts the same mechanism.

declared_assumptions.mass_budget: Supplied favourable engineering.json budget: 55 kg seated adult pilot, 173.9 kg dry mass including pilot, 3.6 kg fuel, 177.5 kg initially wet.
declared_assumptions.not_claimed_from_source: The engine, transmission efficiency, fuel consumption, structural masses, numerical aerodynamic coefficient tables, spring constant and damping values are engineering completions, not Stanley notebook readings.

limitations: Educational reduced model only; not a buildable aircraft design or flight validation.
No unsteady wake, flexible aeroelasticity, structural stress analysis, overlap leakage or section pitching moments.
The source photographs guide proportions and causal principles; missing appendices and exact data remain missing.
